newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks down but steady in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks down but steady in late trade.

text.p: Mexican stocks had halted an earlier slide at mid-afternoon trade on Tuesday as dealing slowed amid a market waiting for Wall Street to define a trend and for the outcome of the primary Cetes auction, dealers said.
"We had some profit-taking this morning, but no one is either buying or selling much at the moment. They're waiting for ADRs to react on Wall Street," a floor trader said.
The leading IPC share index .MXX was down 20.32 points, or 0.52 percent, at 3,964.70. Trading volume .TV.MX was subdued at just 35.8 million shares traded.
"Many buyers are waiting for prices to drop a little more before stepping in," the floor trader added.

Many Mexican ADRs were off despite the recovery by the Dow Jones, which was meanwhile up 37.50 points to 7,383.41. Some dealers said they had lagged behind the Dow, while others said brokers had taken advantage of a weaker peso to settle arbitrage trades.

Telmex ADRs were off 1/4 to 44 in New York, while the telecom firm's L shares were actually up two centavos to 17.42 pesos in Mexico. Telmex accounted for 14 percent of all shares traded in late dealing on the bourse.
"There is also uncertainty over whether Cetes rates can fall again," a desk trader added. "The peso is weak and long bond yields are very high; it's a delicate situation."
The U.S. 30-year Treasury bond was down 16/32 to yield 7.03 percent, while benchmark 48-hour peso contracts had softened by 1.6 centavos to 7.8960/7.9000 per dollar.
Banco de Mexico will announce results of its weekly auction of government securities on Tuesday evening.
